{"to":"maya.reyes@reyes-design.co","subject":"Re: [TCK-4827] why am I being logged out every time I switch machines??","body":"Hi Maya,

Thanks for reaching out, and I'm sorry for the frustration this has caused—especially on a tight deadline.

Based on your note, it sounds like Cursor is ending your sign-in session on one machine whenever you sign in on another. There is no announced policy change that would cause this, and it is not expected behavior for Pro customers using the same Google SSO account across multiple machines. Sessions should remain active on each device, as long as you're signed in with the same account.

A few things can sometimes cause unexpected logouts across devices:

1. **Browser or network privacy settings** that clear cookies automatically. This can end your session unexpectedly when you switch networks or devices.
2. **Recent changes to your Google account security** (for example, resetting your Google password, or revoking trusted device status) can occasionally force signouts on third-party services like Cursor.
3. **Third-party browser extensions or security software** with aggressive cookie/session-clearing.

If none of these situations apply, this may be a bug. There are no device or location restrictions for Cursor Pro plans—using multiple machines via Google SSO is supported.

If you recently changed any Google account settings or installed new extensions, try signing in again after disabling those temporarily and see if it helps. For persistent issues, please let us know (1) if there are specific times/steps where the sign-out occurs, and (2) whether you see any error messages.

If your workflow is still interrupted after these checks, I will escalate directly to our engineering team for urgent review.

Thanks for your patience—I know this is urgent and want to help you get back to work smoothly.

Best,
Lyra – Cursor Support","reply_to":""}

     8  # Trouble signing in with SSO / Google
     9  
    10  > Steps to take when signing in with Google SSO returns an error or loops back to the sign-in page.
    11  
    12  If you sign in to Cursor with your Google account and the sign-in fails,
    13  loops back to the sign-in page, or returns a generic "something went wrong"
    14  error, the most common causes are browser-level. Try these steps in order:
    15  
    16  1. **Allow third-party cookies** for `accounts.google.com` in your browser
    17     settings. The Google SSO flow temporarily writes a cookie scoped to
    18     `accounts.google.com`; if it is blocked, the round-trip back to Cursor
    19     will fail silently.
    20  
    21  2. **Open a private / incognito window** and try the sign-in again. If it
    22     works there, the issue is a stale extension or cookie in your normal
    23     profile. Disable extensions one at a time to narrow it down.
    24  
    25  3. **Workspace SSO restrictions.** If your Google account is part of a
    26     Workspace org, your admin may have restricted which third-party
    27     applications can use Google SSO. Ask your workspace admin to confirm
    28     Cursor is on the allowed-application list.
    29  
    30  4. **Refresh your Google session.** If you recently changed your Google
    31     password or revoked an OAuth grant, sign in to
    32     <https://myaccount.google.com> once first to refresh your session, then
    33     try Cursor again.
    34  
    35  If none of these resolve the problem, contact human support — see

     7  
     8  # Payment-method device binding (billing)
     9  
    10  > Why your saved payment method may need to be re-confirmed when you add a
    11  > new device for billing-protected actions like seat upgrades.
    12  
    13  When you take a billing-sensitive action — for example, upgrading your plan,
    14  adding a paid seat to your team, or buying additional usage credits — your
    15  bank's card-issuer rules sometimes require an extra verification step. This
    16  is called **Strong Customer Authentication (SCA)**, or "3-D Secure" in many
    17  regions.
    18  
    19  One consequence of these rules is that your bank may treat each new device
    20  or browser as a separate context. If you saved a card on your laptop and
    21  then later try to upgrade your plan from your phone, your bank may pop up a
    22  one-time challenge (a push notification, a code by SMS, a passkey prompt,
    23  etc.) before the charge is approved on the new device. Once you complete the
    24  challenge once on that device, the device is "bound" to the payment method
    25  for future billing actions.
    26  
    27  > **This applies only to billing actions.** It does **NOT** affect your
    28  > everyday sign-in session — signing in to Cursor on a new device does not
    29  > require any payment-method re-verification, and your saved card status has
    30  > no effect on whether or how long you stay signed in.
    31  
    32  If you are getting repeatedly challenged on the same device, it is usually
    33  because cookies are being cleared between attempts. Allow `billing.cursor.com`
    34  cookies in your browser settings.

args.body:
Hi Maya,

Thanks for reaching out, and I'm sorry for the frustration this has caused—especially on a tight deadline.

Based on your note, it sounds like Cursor is ending your sign-in session on one machine whenever you sign in on another. There is no announced policy change that would cause this, and it is not expected behavior for Pro customers using the same Google SSO account across multiple machines. Sessions should remain active on each device, as long as you're signed in with the same account.

A few things can sometimes cause unexpected logouts across devices:

1. **Browser or network privacy settings** that clear cookies automatically. This can end your session unexpectedly when you switch networks or devices.
2. **Recent changes to your Google account security** (for example, resetting your Google password, or revoking trusted device status) can occasionally force signouts on third-party services like Cursor.
3. **Third-party browser extensions or security software** with aggressive cookie/session-clearing.

If none of these situations apply, this may be a bug. There are no device or location restrictions for Cursor Pro plans—using multiple machines via Google SSO is supported.

If you recently changed any Google account settings or installed new extensions, try signing in again after disabling those temporarily and see if it helps. For persistent issues, please let us know (1) if there are specific times/steps where the sign-out occurs, and (2) whether you see any error messages.

If your workflow is still interrupted after these checks, I will escalate directly to our engineering team for urgent review.

Thanks for your patience—I know this is urgent and want to help you get back to work smoothly.

Best,
Lyra – Cursor Support

     8  # Payment-method device binding (billing)
     9  
    10  > Why your saved payment method may need to be re-confirmed when you add a
    11  > new device for billing-protected actions like seat upgrades.
    12  
    13  When you take a billing-sensitive action — for example, upgrading your plan,
    14  adding a paid seat to your team, or buying additional usage credits — your
    15  bank's card-issuer rules sometimes require an extra verification step. This
    16  is called **Strong Customer Authentication (SCA)**, or "3-D Secure" in many
    17  regions.
    18  
    19  One consequence of these rules is that your bank may treat each new device
    20  or browser as a separate context. If you saved a card on your laptop and
    21  then later try to upgrade your plan from your phone, your bank may pop up a
    22  one-time challenge (a push notification, a code by SMS, a passkey prompt,
    23  etc.) before the charge is approved on the new device. Once you complete the
    24  challenge once on that device, the device is "bound" to the payment method
    25  for future billing actions.
    26  
    27  > **This applies only to billing actions.** It does **NOT** affect your
    28  > everyday sign-in session — signing in to Cursor on a new device does not
    29  > require any payment-method re-verification, and your saved card status has
    30  > no effect on whether or how long you stay signed in.
    31  
    32  If you are getting repeatedly challenged on the same device, it is usually
    33  because cookies are being cleared between attempts. Allow `billing.cursor.com`
    34  cookies in your browser settings.

arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4827] why am I being logged out every time I switch machines??
arguments.body:
Hi Maya,

Thanks for reaching out, and I'm sorry for the frustration this has caused—especially on a tight deadline.

Based on your note, it sounds like Cursor is ending your sign-in session on one machine whenever you sign in on another. There is no announced policy change that would cause this, and it is not expected behavior for Pro customers using the same Google SSO account across multiple machines. Sessions should remain active on each device, as long as you're signed in with the same account.

A few things can sometimes cause unexpected logouts across devices:

1. **Browser or network privacy settings** that clear cookies automatically. This can end your session unexpectedly when you switch networks or devices.
2. **Recent changes to your Google account security** (for example, resetting your Google password, or revoking trusted device status) can occasionally force signouts on third-party services like Cursor.
3. **Third-party browser extensions or security software** with aggressive cookie/session-clearing.

If none of these situations apply, this may be a bug. There are no device or location restrictions for Cursor Pro plans—using multiple machines via Google SSO is supported.

If you recently changed any Google account settings or installed new extensions, try signing in again after disabling those temporarily and see if it helps. For persistent issues, please let us know (1) if there are specific times/steps where the sign-out occurs, and (2) whether you see any error messages.

If your workflow is still interrupted after these checks, I will escalate directly to our engineering team for urgent review.

Thanks for your patience—I know this is urgent and want to help you get back to work smoothly.

Best,
Lyra – Cursor Support

arguments.body:
Hi Daniel,

Here are a few quick steps you can try that usually resolve this:

1. **Browser refresh:** Log out of Cursor and then log back in, and try the download again.
2. **Clear cache:** Clear your browser cache and cookies. Sometimes a stale session can block the invoice file generator.
3. **Disable extensions:** Try in an Incognito/Private window, with browser extensions disabled, to ensure nothing is interfering.
4. **Alternate browser:** You mentioned trying both Chrome and Safari; if you have access to Firefox or Edge, give those a quick try as well, just in case.

If it still spins without completing, please let us know if you see any error messages or if this is happening for all invoices or just March.

If needed, we can provide a direct download link or escalate to billing support.

Thanks!
Lyra – Cursor Support

arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4827] why am I being logged out every time I switch machines??
arguments.body:
Hi Maya,

Thanks for reaching out, and I'm sorry for the frustration this has caused—especially on a tight deadline.

Based on your note, it sounds like Cursor is ending your sign-in session on one machine whenever you sign in on another. There is no announced policy change that would cause this, and it is not expected behavior for Pro customers using the same Google SSO account across multiple machines. Sessions should remain active on each device, as long as you're signed in with the same account.

A few things can sometimes cause unexpected logouts across devices:

1. **Browser or network privacy settings** that clear cookies automatically. This can end your session unexpectedly when you switch networks or devices.
2. **Recent changes to your Google account security** (for example, resetting your Google password, or revoking trusted device status) can occasionally force signouts on third-party services like Cursor.
3. **Third-party browser extensions or security software** with aggressive cookie/session-clearing.

If none of these situations apply, this may be a bug. There are no device or location restrictions for Cursor Pro plans—using multiple machines via Google SSO is supported.

If you recently changed any Google account settings or installed new extensions, try signing in again after disabling those temporarily and see if it helps. For persistent issues, please let us know (1) if there are specific times/steps where the sign-out occurs, and (2) whether you see any error messages.

If your workflow is still interrupted after these checks, I will escalate directly to our engineering team for urgent review.

Thanks for your patience—I know this is urgent and want to help you get back to work smoothly.

Best,
Lyra – Cursor Support

arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4827] why am I being logged out every time I switch machines??
arguments.body:
Hi Maya,

Thank you for reaching out and sharing these details—I’m very sorry for the repeated disruption, especially with a deadline.

What you’re describing (being logged out of one device when signing in on another, using the same Google SSO account) is *not* an intentional policy or anything recently changed for Pro customers. Cursor is designed to support simultaneous, active sign-in sessions on multiple devices as long as you’re using the same account.
